title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: You get a list of integers. Return a new list where each position holds the product of all the other numbers, everything except the one at that position. Do not use division, and aim for a single pass in each direction.

example.caption: For index 2 the others are 1, 2 and 4. Their product is 8.

idea.sentence: Everything except nums[i] is the product on its left times the product on its right. Sweep left to right for the first part, then right to left for the second.

jargon.plain: The product of all numbers before index i.
The product of all numbers after index i.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of numbers, e.g. [1,2,3,4]

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

compare.bruteLabel: Multiply all the others, per index

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: For each index, multiply the other n minus 1 numbers.

rows.name: Total divided by self
rows.note: Not allowed here, and it breaks when a zero is in the list.

rows.name: Prefix and suffix sweeps
rows.note: Two passes with two running numbers. The output list does not count as extra space.

fast.takeaway: Each answer splits into a left part and a right part. A running product gives each part for free, one step at a time.

stages.title: Start the output
stages.note: The output list is the only storage. Its slots will be filled by two sweeps.

stages.title: Left sweep
stages.note: Store in out[i] the product of everything left of i. Then fold nums[i] into the running prefix.

stages.title: Right sweep
stages.note: Multiply out[i] by the product of everything right of i. Then fold nums[i] into the running suffix.

edges.title: One zero
edges.why: Only the zero's own slot is nonzero, because every other slot includes the zero in its product.

edges.title: Two zeros
edges.why: Every slot has a zero among the others. All answers are zero.

edges.title: Two numbers
edges.why: Each slot is just the other number. Prefix and suffix start at one, the empty product.

edges.title: Zero at the start
edges.why: The prefix is 1 for index 0, but becomes 0 for the rest. The suffix part then rescues index 0.

gotchas.text: Dividing the total by nums[i] fails on zeros, since you cannot divide by zero and the total itself becomes zero. The sweeps never divide.
A product of 0 and a negative number gives -0 in JavaScript. -0 === 0 is true, but Object.is(-0, 0) is false and a deep-equals helper may complain. Only strict comparisons with Object.is notice it.
Numbers are doubles. Products stay exact only up to 2^53 − 1. This problem promises results fit in 32 bits, so it is fine here.
int is 64-bit on 64-bit machines. It does not overflow here, but on a 32-bit build a large product could.

recap.key: The answer at i is the product on its left times the product on its right. Build the left parts going right, then multiply the right parts in going left.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(1) beyond the output.
moves: Left to right: store the running product, then grow it
Right to left: multiply by the running product, then grow it
